+# Conventional Commits
+
+Generate a Conventional Commit message following [Conventional Commits v1.0.0](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/#summary).
+
+## Rules
+
+- Use one of: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `perf`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`
+- Format: `type(optional-scope): subject` (max 72 chars)
+- Subject: lowercase, imperative, no trailing period
+- Body (optional):
+  - Use a concise summary of the changes
+  - Prefer describing what changed over why it changed
+  - When listing multiple items, use bullet points for clarity
+
+## When to use bullet points
+
+- Use bullet points in the commit body when you need to list multiple distinct items (e.g., changed files, individual fixes, migration steps, or breaking changes).
+- Prefer bullets when each item is short, independent, and can be read out of order.
+- Avoid bullets for single-sentence summaries or flowing prose—use plain sentences instead.
+- Keep bullets concise, use imperative fragments, and avoid trailing periods; keep lines within ~72 characters when possible.
+- Use a simple, consistent bullet style (e.g., `- item`) to improve readability in changelogs and review diffs.
+
+## Footer (optional):
+
+- Use `BREAKING CHANGE: ...` for breaking changes
+- Reference issues with `refs #123`
+- Return only a concise commit message (summary and optional body), without additional commentary.
